entries.why_wrong: You're treating this as a print-ordering issue, but where `console.log` sits relative to the recursive call has no effect on whether recursion ever stops. The crash comes from `n` sailing past `0` for odd starting values, not from when the number gets printed.

Swapping to `n - 1` isn't a performance tweak here — the step size determines whether `n` can ever land exactly on `0`. The real issue is that `n - 2` skips over `0` entirely for odd inputs, so the base case never fires, not that the countdown runs slowly.

`countDown` is meant to run for its side effects (the `console.log` calls), so not returning a value is normal and isn't what crashes the program. The crash is a stack overflow from recursion that never reaches its base case, which is unrelated to return values.

Calling `countDown(n)` with no decrement would make every call recurse forever, but that's not the bug described — this function actually works for even inputs and only fails for odd ones. The real flaw is that `n - 2` can jump past `0` without ever equaling it, not that `n` fails to change at all.
